why: The measured failure, as a case. Asked three times during ENT-235 which GDPR article requires a record of processing activities, the 2B tier answered 50, then 34, then 54. It is 30, and every answer was schema-valid, well formed and confidently wrong. The grammar guarantees the shape and nothing guarantees the content.
signal: We are a 40 person recruitment agency in Tallinn. We keep candidate CVs for two years, run reference checks by email, and store interview notes in a shared drive.

obligations.title: Records of Processing Activities (ROPA)
obligations.summary: Article 30 GDPR: controllers and processors must maintain a written record of the processing under their responsibility, covering purposes, categories of data subjects and data, recipients, transfers, retention and security measures.

obligations.title: Security of Processing
obligations.summary: Article 32 GDPR: controllers and processors must implement technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, taking account of the state of the art, the cost of implementation and the nature of the processing.

weak.response: {"narrative": "You keep candidate CVs and interview notes, so you must maintain a written record of that processing under Article 50 of the GDPR, including retention periods and who the data is shared with.", "citations": ["gdpr-art-50-ropa"], "confident": true}

strong.response: {"narrative": "You keep candidate CVs and interview notes for two years, so you need a written record of that processing: what you collect, why you collect it, how long you keep it and who else sees it. Reference checks by email send data to people outside the agency, and those recipients belong in the record too.", "citations": ["gdpr-art-30-ropa"], "confident": true}

why: gdpr-art-35-dpia is a real obligation in the corpus, and it was not among the ones this run was shown. Validating against the corpus would accept it; validating against the offered set refuses it, because the model produced it from somewhere other than its context, which is exactly what the validator exists to catch.
signal: We run a mental health app that scores users for relapse risk from their diary entries, and we are rolling it out to 30000 people.

obligations.title: Records of Processing Activities (ROPA)
obligations.summary: Article 30 GDPR: controllers and processors must maintain a written record of the processing under their responsibility, covering purposes, categories of data subjects and data, recipients, transfers, retention and security measures.

weak.response: {"narrative": "Scoring users for relapse risk at this scale is high risk processing of health data, so you must carry out a data protection impact assessment before you launch.", "citations": ["gdpr-art-35-dpia"], "confident": true}

strong.response: {"narrative": "You process diary entries and risk scores about identifiable users, so you need a written record of that processing before the rollout: the purposes, who the data is about, how long you keep it and who it goes to.", "citations": ["gdpr-art-30-ropa"], "confident": true}
